intro: Notion works well for technical writers on Mac, as long as you treat it as a wiki with owners and dates. Turn a page into a wiki, nest your docs under it, and use Owner and Verification to track who maintains each page. Lazur, a voice assistant that lives in the Mac notch, answers questions and walks you through steps while you work in the Notion desktop app.
tldr: Turn any page into a wiki from the page menu with Turn into Wiki.
Use the Owner and Verification properties to see who must renew each page and when.
Exports lose structure. Callouts need HTML, and only the current database view exports.
The Mac desktop app needs macOS 13 or later. Notion recommends the latest macOS release.
Lazur points, explains and walks you through each click. It does not click for you.

blocks.text: Most technical writers on Mac use Notion as a team wiki first and a writing tool second. The hard part is not the first draft. It is keeping dozens of pages accurate after the product changes. That means knowing who owns each page, when it expires, and how to get the content out when a publishing tool or a customer needs it. This guide walks through those jobs in the order you hit them.
Set up a Notion wiki for technical writers on Mac

Start with the right app. The Notion desktop app for Mac needs macOS 13 or above, and Notion recommends the latest version of the operating system. To check yours, open the Apple menu and choose About This Mac. If your Mac runs an older release, the desktop app will not install, so use Notion in a browser until you can update.

Next, decide where the wiki lives. Put it in a teamspace so the docs stay apart from drafts, meeting notes, and personal pages. Notion's team wiki guide suggests two starting points. You can pick the Product wiki or Engineering wiki template from the template gallery, or create a top-level page in a teamspace and nest sub-pages under it.

Already have a page you want as the front door? Open the page menu and choose Turn into Wiki. The page gains wiki properties. Then add child pages under it, one for each topic, so the wiki has a clear tree that readers can follow.

blocks.title: Templates bring properties
blocks.text: The product and engineering templates add properties on day one. Read the Owner and Verification columns before you fill in pages. Delete or rename anything your team does not use, so nobody skips a field by accident.
Owner and Verification: the two wiki properties that matter

A Notion wiki comes with four default properties. Owner is a person. Last edited date updates on its own. Tags is a multi-select field. Verification is unique to wikis, and you can set it to an expiry date or to infinite. Most of your daily review work happens in Owner and Verification, so set those two first.

Verification is the part people miss. When a verification expires, the page owner gets a notification and must review and renew it. Only the page owner of that specific page can verify it. That rule keeps one name on every page, which matters on a team where people change roles.

Here is a practical rule. Set Verification to the date of your next release. A page for a login flow that changes in March should expire in March, not in a year. Infinite is fine for stable reference pages such as a glossary, but use it sparingly. Otherwise the field stops telling you anything useful.
Find stale and unverified pages in Notion

Notion's wiki guide gives four checks you can run from a database view. Sort by Verification to see what expires next. Filter for unverified or expired pages to find the gaps. Filter by tag when you update one topic. Sort by Last edited date to find content nobody has touched.

items: Open the wiki database and select the view you use for review.
Click Sort in the view toolbar, choose Verification, then pick ascending order.
Click Filter and set a condition on Verification for expired or unverified pages.
Rename the view so your team can find it, such as Expiring soon.

blocks.text: Filters belong to the view, not to the page. If you need one view for each team, duplicate the view and change its filter. For the full walkthrough, read [how to filter a database in Notion on Mac](/how-to/filter-a-database-in-notion).

blocks.title: Last edited is not accuracy
blocks.text: Sorting by last edited date finds pages nobody touched. It does not find pages that are wrong. A page edited last week can still describe an old login flow. Verification is the better signal for accuracy.
Export Notion pages on Mac without losing content

Exports are where technical writers lose the most time. Notion's export help says a full-page database exports as a CSV file, with a Markdown file for each subpage. Callout blocks export as HTML, because Markdown has no equivalent. If your publishing tool reads only Markdown, test one callout before you run the full export.

The view matters too. Database exports include only the current view or the default view. You cannot export all views at once. Form views cannot be exported at all. Switch to the view you need, export it, then open the file and check it before you trust it.

blocks.text: To export one page, open the page menu, choose Export, then pick a format. The full steps live in [how to export a page in Notion on Mac](/how-to/export-a-page-in-notion).
Full workspace export and download limits

A full workspace export lives under Settings > General > Export all workspace content. Notion says it can take up to 30 hours to process, depending on workspace size. The download link expires after 7 days. Start a full export well before a handoff, not the afternoon it is due.

blocks.title: Save the zip on day one
blocks.text: When the export email arrives, download the file the same day. If the link expires, you must start the export again and wait for it to process. Keep a dated copy in your own storage.
PDF and printing from the Mac app

The Notion desktop app has no print option. Full-page databases cannot be printed from a browser either. Export the page to PDF first, open the PDF in Preview, then press ⌘ P to print. If a PDF export fails, Notion exports the page as HTML instead, so open that file in a browser and print from there.

PDF export with subpages is a Business or Enterprise feature. On Free or Plus, export each page on its own. Name the files with a version and a date, so your handoff folder does not drift away from the wiki.
Keyboard shortcuts for Notion on Mac

items: ⌘ P: quick find, jump to any page by name
/: open the block menu on an empty line
⌘ Z: undo the last change
⇧ ⌘ Z: redo
⌘ C and ⌘ V: copy and paste text in the page
Hold ⌥ ⌘: ask Lazur about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud

blocks.text: Mac users often expect one search box for everything. Use Notion's search for the whole workspace, and use the page's own tools for the text on one page. Search tips are covered in [how to search your workspace in Notion on Mac](/how-to/search-your-workspace-in-notion).
Check the Mac app version and recent changes

Notion's release notes list high contrast mode from July 30, 2026. It works on desktop and web. You turn it on at Settings > Preferences > Appearance. The October 2026 entries focus on agents and version history. None of the recent entries names a change to the Mac app, so do not assume a menu moved without checking.
Notion pricing and page history for writing teams

Notion's pricing page lists four plans. Free is $0, Plus is $10, Business is $20, and Enterprise is custom. Prices are per member per month. Yearly billing saves up to 20%. Check the pricing page before you buy, because the monthly and yearly toggle changes the number you see.

blocks.caption: Plan limits from Notion's pricing page.

blocks.text: History matters for docs. If you rewrite a page on a Tuesday and need the old version a month later, a Free workspace may not keep it. Business keeps page history for 90 days. SAML SSO is included on Business and Enterprise, and it is not included on Free or Plus.
Ask Lazur for help while you write in Notion

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac, and it lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. While you hold the shortcut, Lazur looks at the screen, points at things and answers out loud. Ask where a control is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it.

Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it moves to the next step. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. You stay in control of the page.

Dictation helps with docs too. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app, including a Notion page. Add product names to your personal dictionary once, so dictation spells them the way you expect. Snippets and clipboard slots handle boilerplate, such as a standard warning or a version footer.
Mistakes technical writers make in Notion

items: Treating Notion as the public site. Helpview argues that Notion gives limited control over titles, descriptions, slugs and social previews.
Mixing drafts and public pages in one place. Helpview says those workspaces need strict boundaries. Put public pages in their own teamspace.
Leaving Verification blank. A page with no expiry never prompts anyone to review it.
Exporting the wrong view. The export carries only the current or default view.
Assuming history lasts. Free keeps page history for 7 days, so save a copy before a big rewrite.
Looking for print in the Mac app. The desktop app has no print option, so export to PDF first.

blocks.text: How much sync work the survey shows

The State of Docs 2026 survey had 1,131 respondents across the documentation industry. Technical writers were the largest group at 35%, but not a majority. Across all respondents, 30% named keeping docs in sync as their single biggest workflow challenge. That share rose to 43% for engineers and sat at 26% for technical writers.

Read that chart with care. The survey covers documentation people in general, not Notion users or Mac users. No survey found in this research splits results by tool or platform. Still, the sync problem explains why Verification matters. Owners and expiry dates give you a schedule for checking pages, which a wiki alone does not do.
What to do next with your Notion docs

items: Check that your Mac runs macOS 13 or later, then install the desktop app.
Turn one page into a wiki and add two child pages under it.
Fill Owner and Verification on every page before you add more pages.
Run the expiring-soon view once a week, and rename it for your team.
Export one page to PDF and check the callouts before any handoff.

blocks.text: If you want Lazur on your Mac, [download the app](/download) and try the hold-to-ask shortcut on a Notion page. Compare plans on the [pricing page](/pricing) before you commit. Lazur only looks at the screen while you hold the shortcut.

faq.question: Does Notion for technical writers on Mac need a specific macOS version?
faq.answer: Yes. The Notion desktop app for Mac needs macOS 13 or above, and Notion recommends the latest macOS release. If your Mac is older, use Notion in a browser instead. Check the system requirements page before you install the desktop app.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Notion pages for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur guides you, points at things, explains, answers out loud, drafts text and dictates text at the cursor. It does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. You make each change, and Lazur helps you find the right control.

faq.question: Why did my Notion export come out as many files?
faq.answer: A full-page database exports as a CSV file, plus a Markdown file for each subpage. Notion's export help describes it that way. Plan for the extra files when you hand the export to another tool.

faq.question: How do I print a Notion page from the Mac app?
faq.answer: The desktop app has no print option. Export the page to PDF, open the file in Preview, and press ⌘ P. If the PDF export fails, Notion exports the page as HTML, so open that file in a browser and print from there.

faq.question: What happens when a wiki page verification expires?
faq.answer: The page owner gets a notification and must review and renew the verification. Only the page owner of that specific page can verify it. Filter for expired pages to find the ones nobody has renewed yet.

faq.question: Which Notion plan keeps page history the longest?
faq.answer: Business keeps page history for 90 days, according to Notion's pricing page. Plus keeps 30 days, and Free keeps 7 days. Enterprise is listed as custom. Check the pricing page for current details before you choose.

faq.question: Does Lazur connect to Notion?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It is not a plugin or add-in for Notion or any other app. Use it alongside Notion, not inside it.

faq.question: Is there a survey about technical writers who use Notion?
faq.answer: Not one that this research found. The State of Docs 2026 survey covers documentation people in general. It names technical writers as the largest role at 35%, but it does not split results by tool or by platform.
